🔁 THE MONEY MOVES BEFORE WE DO

Most people ask the same question first, and it isn't about strategy. It's who carries the risk.

Here's the order, and it never changes:

✔️ Nothing paid to us upfront
✔️ You buy the evaluation in your own name
✔️ The desk trades it — you don't touch the terminal
✔️ The payout lands in your account
✔️ Then we invoice our share

🫡 If the evaluation fails, you're out the evaluation fee and we've worked for free.

🪙 That's the deal. It's the only version of it we'd take ourselves. 🪙

📄 STATIC, NOT TRAILING

The drawdown rule is where most evaluations are quietly lost. Not on a bad trade — on a clause.

Most firms trail the limit behind your equity. Make money, and the floor rises with you. Give a little back and you breach an account that's still in profit.

🫡 Ours doesn't move. The floor is set on day one and stays there.

🪙 Read the drawdown clause before you read the profit target. It decides more of your outcome. 🪙

posty.body:
🧾 RECEIPTS, NOT SCREENSHOTS

Anyone can post a dashboard. A dashboard proves that software can draw a number.

🫡 What we post instead is the paperwork:every payout that goes out gets a certificate with a name, an amount, a date and a link anyone can open and check.

We don't publish the good weeks and quietly skip the rest. They go up as they happen, in order.

🪙 A number you can't click is just a number. 🪙

💰 MEET JAMES — $17,477. Verified.

James has been trading since before most prop firms existed. He didn't need teaching. He needed capital that wasn't his pension.

🫡 The certificate was the part he asked about first. Every payout gets one — name, amount, date, and a link anyone can check.

🪙 $17,477, issued and paid. 🪙

He'd tell you the strategy is the easy part. Finding someone who pays on time is not.

🎥 HE HAD NEVER OPENED A PROP ACCOUNT

Six months ago Mike couldn't have told you what a pip was. He says so himself in the first ten seconds — which is why we're posting the clip instead of writing the story.

🫡 What he brought wasn't a strategy. It was a willingness to read the contract and ask what happens if it goes wrong.

✔️ No trading background
✔️ Evaluation bought in his own name
✔️ The desk traded it — he never touched the terminal
✔️ He scaled into a larger account after the first payout

🪙 He spent the whole time waiting for a catch. He talks about that longer than he talks about the money. 🪙

The figure on screen is his, not ours. Watch him say it.

🎥 SHE TELLS IT, NOT HIM

This one comes from Ryan's wife, and that's the part worth your minute.

Angelina spent years watching him trade their savings. She says the losses were never the hard part — it was sitting in the same room knowing what was on the line every time he opened a position.

🫡 Then he stopped using their money and cleared an evaluation instead, on the same strategy he'd been running for years.

✔️ Same trader
✔️ Same strategy
✔️ Different money behind it

🪙 What changed at home wasn't the income. It was that a bad week stopped being a household problem. 🪙

She names the figure in the clip. We'd rather she said it than us.

🎥 HE COUNTED THE HOURS

Dave already traded futures and crypto and ran a small signals group. He didn't need teaching. His own capital just scaled too slowly to matter.

🫡 The firms he'd tried before felt built for him to fail — trailing drawdowns, consistency rules nobody mentions until you break one.

✔️ Cleared the evaluation on his own setups
✔️ Nothing about how he trades changed
✔️ The first payout was processed inside a day

🪙 He counts the hours out loud in the clip. That is the entire review. 🪙

Watch it before you compare us to anyone on a marketing page.
